summary: Tested the technique score engine (ca-score-v2) and ball tracking (ca-ball-v1) end to end: unit and edge-case tests, score-check reproducibility and authz, dashboard/saved-report/PDF consistency (PDF rendered with pymupdf), ball accuracy against ground truth (t_fast, t_exit), phase-marker integrity, failure tolerance, media Range, the viewer UI in Playwright (desktop and 390px mobile) and a full e2e run with bat.mp4. Nearly everything passes. One real frontend bug: the viewer labels about 1/3 of frames one frame early while playing or scrubbing WebM, so the readout and ball marker belong to the previous frame. One real backend issue: basic-plan locked metric values leak through score.inputs and score.metric_scores.

minor.issue: For report_level basic, b.metrics values are locked (value=None, 'Upgrade to view measured metrics.'), but b.score.inputs[*].value and b.score.metric_scores[*].value still contain the raw measured values. This leaks plan-gated data. Reproduced by calling filter_report directly.

Each Range request loads the whole object into memory (get_object) and then slices it. Chromium sent 3 range requests (bytes=0-) for a 1.8 MB clip. Fine for small clips, but memory- and IO-heavy for larger videos. Correctness is fine: 206/416/403 all verified.

When pose status is 'unavailable', both the PDF (continue at report_pdf.py:191) and the frontend (Angle early return) skip the ball tracking block, even though ball tracking runs independently and may have results.

ui_bugs.issue: frame = Math.floor(t*fps + 1e-3). requestVideoFrameCallback mediaTime is millisecond-quantised for WebM (measured: 2.733, 3.133, 3.233, so x30 = 81.99, 93.99, 96.99), so frames 82, 94, 97 and others are labelled as 81, 93, 96 and the PREVIOUS frame's ball detection and marker are drawn over the current image. Reproduced: scrubbing to 127/30 s (the 'best' detection, conf 0.88) shows 'frame 126 / ball conf 0.79'; then viewer-next-frame jumps from 126 to 128. Fix: use a larger epsilon, e.g. Math.floor(t*fps + 0.1), or Math.round(mediaTime*fps) for rVFC times. Stepping from a plain currentTime seek (viewer-next-frame / viewer-prev-frame starting at 2.6 s) did advance exactly one frame: 79, 80, 81, 82, 83, 84 forward and 83, 82, 81 back.

design_issues.screen: PDF page 1 header vs score block
issues: Two different 'keypoint confidence' numbers on page 1: the header says 0.7 (quality.keypoint_confidence, median of key joints) while the evidence box says 'keypoint conf 0.57' (mean of included-metric confidences). Label them distinctly.
The note says 'bat and ball are not tracked', which contradicts the new ball tracking feature; it should say the bat is not tracked and ball contact is not determined.

Viewer: loading spinner clears; at currentTime 2.6 the readout shows frame 78 and ball conf 0.23; scrubber seeks; ball and skeleton toggles clear and restore the canvas pixels (1477 yellow pixels to 0 and back); overlay-legend present (x2); phase-ball-toggle swaps 4 phase images (ball overlay to pose overlay; setup has no ball, so it is unchanged); ball-summary shows 96/210, 45.7%, 0.88 at 4.233s; filming tip present
Mobile 390px: no horizontal page overflow (the metrics table scrolls inside its overflow-x-auto card by design)
action_items: Fix the AnalysisViewer frame index: Math.floor(t*fps + 1e-3) gives an off-by-one with ms-quantised rVFC mediaTime. Use Math.floor(t*fps + 0.1) or round the mediaTime.
filter_report: when metrics are locked (lvl<1), also strip values from score.inputs and score.metric_scores (or drop them).
Show the ball summary in the PDF and UI even when pose is unavailable.
Reword the impact phase note ('bat and ball are not tracked') and disambiguate the two keypoint-confidence numbers on PDF page 1.
critical_code_review_comments: ball_pipeline: overlapping tracks can produce two observed detections on the same frame. phase_marker takes the first one and the frontend Map keeps the last one, so they can disagree. This is rare.
AnalysisViewer: the rVFC effect depends on draw, which changes every frame, so the callback is cancelled and re-registered on every frame during playback. It works, but it is churn.

AnalysisViewer: there is no timeout on the loading state. Under backend CPU load (during the ball test) one run stayed on viewer-loading for more than 30s; it loaded in about 5s once the CPU was idle.
score_engine: strongest and opportunities can name the same metric when there are few metrics with scores of 80-90.

pose_pipeline uses seek-based reads (CAP_PROP_POS_FRAMES) for idx, while ball_pipeline reads sequentially. On VFR/B-frame codecs the indices can drift, so phase.idx and ball.frame may not refer to the same image.

success_rate.backend: 100% of tests (27/27 new + 7/7 existing); 1 data-leak issue found by code review and reproduced
